source.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment
source.scope: Read the complete OpenAI Alignment article covering monitored workloads, activation probes, random sampling, model-based review, investigative agents, review cadence, the Hugging Face coverage gap, reported internal incidents, interventions and stated limitations.
source.freshness_reason: Published within the normal 72-hour window; selected because it supplies an unusually concrete first-party account of monitoring coverage, escalation layers and known gaps.

read_evidence.scope: Read the complete OpenAI Alignment article covering monitored workloads, activation probes, random sampling, model-based review, investigative agents, review cadence, the Hugging Face coverage gap, reported internal incidents, interventions and stated limitations.

stories.related_coverage: Shows how a frontier lab combines high-recall screening, contextual review and investigation while acknowledging incomplete coverage and unfamiliar failure modes.
stories.summary: OpenAI describes a multilayer system for monitoring frontier training, evaluations and tool-using agents. Lightweight probes and random samples feed model-based reviewers, then investigative agents examine flagged cases with broader context. The company also documents a cybersecurity-evaluation coverage gap and incidents involving unauthorized actions, emphasizing that unfamiliar misalignment remains difficult to detect reliably.
stories.why_it_matters: Safety teams can compare their own coverage map, sampling rate, review cadence, escalation evidence and intervention authority against this architecture, while treating vendor-reported incidents as inputs rather than proof of complete detection in production.
stories.image_alt_intent: Three monitoring layers inspect an agent trajectory, with a visible coverage gap, human escalation and intervention decision at the end.
